assets: cash (United Arab Emirates dirhams, in a safe)
description: A bitcoin trader was attacked at his home in the Naif district of Dubai by four men who used a false pretext of a wrong address to force entry, threatened him with a knife at his throat, then tied his hands and feet with plastic rope before retrieving the key to a safe hidden under a table. The attackers stole AED 1.7 million belonging to the victim's business partner, who discovered the scene after being alerted by phone. Having entered the country illegally, the four suspects were arrested and confessed to the facts; on appeal (September 2022), they were sentenced to 3 years in prison each and a joint fine of AED 1.7 million, with deportation upon completion of their sentence.
victims: A bitcoin trader (identity not disclosed), resident in Dubai
outcome: Part of the stolen sum was recovered in the suspects' possession; the 4 attackers were sentenced to 3 years in prison each and a joint fine of AED 1.7 million (upheld by the Dubai Court of Appeal in September 2022), followed by deportation from the country.
target_reason: Khaleej Times states only that the AED 1.7 million was in "a safe that belonged to his trading partner": the source does not say whether this cash was the partner's private funds or the shared treasury of a two-person trading operation (the victim was therefore not acting "alone and on his own behalf"). No company is named, but nothing allows one to state that this was purely personal wealth either: undetermined.

city: Bukit Timah, King Albert Park, Singapore
amount: approximately S$4,341,328 (~US$3.2 million) in cash, cryptocurrency and valuables
description: On the night of April 18, 2024, a group of at least five men armed with machetes (parangs) and baseball bats broke into a luxury bungalow (GCB) along King Albert Park, in Bukit Timah, robbing eleven people present (aged 25-45) of a total haul of approximately S$4.34 million (~US$3.2 million) in cash (SGD, USD, dirhams), cryptocurrency (USDT) and luxury watches (Richard Mille, Rolex). The hardest-hit victim, a 29-year-old woman, lost more than S$3.9 million alone, including nearly US$2.64 million in Tether (USDT). Five Malaysians were charged with armed robbery in a gang after being arrested in Singapore or extradited from Malaysia, two of them having fled to Johor Bahru before being handed over to the Singapore police in late April.
victims: Eleven victims aged 25 to 45 (identities undisclosed), the most heavily robbed being a 29-year-old woman
outcome: Judgment of 14 September 2026: six Malaysians sentenced (a seventh, Muhammad Yusuf Kassim, is at large): Wong Chi Shan and Goh Boon Tong 12 years 11 months in prison and 24 strokes of the cane, Mohd Hamidon Ahmed 10 and a half years, Mohd Hashim Ismail 8 years 8 months, Kartik Palaniappan and Muhammad Tauffiq Ahmad Fauzi 7 years 8 months. The cryptocurrency had been transferred from the host's phone to a wallet controlled by the robbers; police recovered about S$1.69 million in crypto.
target_reason: The charge sheets detail individual losses (USDT in personal accounts, cash, Richard Mille/Rolex watches, Ferrari key) suffered by private individuals in a private residence; no commercial entity is mentioned as a victim.

amount: Unknown (personal funds, treasury and undistributed profits of Revelo Intel, Revelo Ventures funds)
description: Nick Drakon, CEO of the crypto research platform Revelo Intel, revealed in a message posted on X on September 5, 2024 that he had been the victim of a home invasion: an organized group held him at gunpoint and threatened his wife and their eight-month-old son to force him to empty his wallets and log into several custodial crypto accounts. The stolen funds mixed his personal assets with the treasury and undistributed profits of Revelo Intel and Revelo Ventures funds pending settlement; Drakon suggested there were signs of inside involvement within Revelo Ventures. He resigned in favor of COO Vu Benson, gave up his equity stake, and promised 30% of future profits to affected investors; no arrests have been reported.
victims: Nick Drakon, CEO of Revelo Intel, his wife, and their 8-month-old son
outcome: Personal and company crypto assets stolen; CEO resigned; no arrest reported
target_reason: The stolen funds mixed the CEO's personal assets with the treasury/undistributed profits of Revelo Intel and Revelo Ventures funds, with the corporate share being the more detailed and larger portion.

amount: EUR 9,689 taken (withdrawals at Geldmaat with his card + transfers from his ING account to buy bitcoins on an account opened in his name under duress); total material damages awarded by the court: EUR 10,546.24 (including EUR 9,998 in amounts taken)
description: On the night of November 27-28, 2021, a man lured via Instagram into an Amsterdam hotel room was surprised naked in the bathroom by about seven attackers, one of them armed with a knife: bound with tape then handcuffed, gagged, his head covered with a taped towel, he spent the night locked in the toilet under the guard of two men, with a knife held to his throat to make him give up his banking codes. Forced to call ING claiming he wanted to buy bitcoins in order to get his account unblocked, he saw 8,698 euros transferred between 00:04 and 05:36 to a cryptocurrency platform where a verified account had been opened in his name; the verification selfie, later handed over to police by the platform, shows him bare-chested and handcuffed. One of the participants was sentenced on January 11, 2024 by the Amsterdam court to 3 years in prison for these acts and two other violent robberies.
victims: A man referred to as "aangever 2" in the judgment (identity protected), lured via Instagram
outcome: EUR 8,698 converted to cryptocurrency + EUR 1,000 withdrawn; at least one defendant sentenced on January 11, 2024 by the Amsterdam court to 3 years in prison for these acts and two other violent robberies (Sadiyat and Segam investigations)
target_reason: A private individual lured via Instagram is forced to transfer funds from his personal bank account to a crypto account opened in his name.
source1_name: Rechtbank Amsterdam, judgment ECLI:NL:RBAMS:2024:110 of 11 January 2024 (Rechtspraak.nl, official judicial source)
source2_name: Rechtspraak.nl — accessible version of the same judgment

city: Taoyuan (empty lot near a Hi-Life convenience store; district redacted in the judgment)
amount: TWD 350,000 in cash and two phones
description: Lin Su-hsia (林素霞), whom scammers had convinced that she had to buy cryptocurrency to pay a tax, had been given the LINE contact of a "crypto dealer", Chiang Yu-hsiang. Learning that she would come to buy TWD 350,000 worth of crypto, he decided to rob her and recruited a friend, Chen Po-hao, and a minor. At around 3:30 p.m. on 14 January 2025 in Taoyuan, while she waited on an empty lot near the convenience store where they were to meet, the minor snatched her phone and her handbag containing the TWD 350,000; she held on to the bag and was dragged some distance before letting go. The trio, who had come from Taichung by high-speed rail and car, split the loot in a toilet at Taipei high-speed rail station.
victims: Lin Su-hsia (林素霞), a private crypto buyer who had already been scammed
outcome: The Taoyuan District Court (114年度訴字第801號, 30 October 2025) found robbery with violence, since the victim had been dragged: Chiang 7 years 6 months, Chen 5 years 10 months; the minor was dealt with by the Taichung juvenile court. The High Court dismissed Chiang's appeal on 30 April 2026 (115年度上訴字第739號).
target_reason: A private individual who came with her cash to buy crypto from a so-called dealer and was robbed by him.
source1_name: Tribunal de district de Taoyuan, 114年度訴字第801號 (30.10.2025)

amount: over GBP 800 in cryptocurrency plus GBP 377 in cash (up to GBP 30,000 expected by the attackers)
description: On 2 September 2022 at around 7 p.m., a teenager who had come to buy nitrous oxide outside the SnowHill Snooker Centre in Digbeth was knocked unconscious by a blow to the head and then dragged into a Volkswagen by four young men. Taken to Oldbury, he was subjected to about two hours of abuse — a fake sawn-off shotgun, a machete, punches and blows with a metal can, repeated death threats — while his attackers posted videos on his Snapchat demanding a ransom of up to GBP 30,000 from his friends. Finding no funds, they took GBP 377, his phone, and his trainers, and forced him to convert over GBP 800 in cryptocurrency before abandoning him at a train station; Nyckyle Harris, Panashe Mahachi, Daejon Byfield, and Danreiko Henry were sentenced on 18 August 2023 by Birmingham Crown Court to nearly 40 years in prison combined.
outcome: approx. GBP 800 in crypto and GBP 377 stolen; Nyckyle Harris, Panashe Mahachi, Danreiko Henry, and Daejon Byfield sentenced to nearly 40 years in prison combined (Birmingham Crown Court, 18 August 2023)
target_reason: A teenager was abducted and forced to convert his own personal cryptocurrency to pay a ransom.

description: From February 2021 to February 2022, Kim (35), a former organized-crime member, forced an IT company CEO into a bitcoin "investment" then unilaterally demanded a 30% return, extorting approximately KRW 14.6 billion (of which KRW 4.86 billion was formally established) from the victim, his employees, his family and his associates. At least 19 incidents of violence were recorded: confinement under permanent surveillance in a Gangnam hotel, threats of acid attacks against the victim's parents, and, in early February 2022, the confinement of two employees for 13 hours in a Nonhyeon-dong office where they were beaten with a baseball bat and threatened with a knife. The 16 gang members were arrested between February and early May 2023, 8 of them placed in detention.
note: The sources establish an aim other than obtaining cryptocurrency: a debt, a dispute or a business conflict.

description: Between March 28 and April 2, 2021, Zhang (a repeat offender sentenced in 2007 to 18 years for kidnapping, rape and robbery, released in May 2020) and his accomplices Zhang A and Liu forcibly took the victim Cui to woods near Baipenyao, Fengtai district, in Beijing. Under threat of a knife, bound and beaten, she was forced to buy 2.529 bitcoins for RMB 936,000 and then transfer them by scanning a QR code to an anonymous wallet; the accomplices later resold them for RMB 930,247 and split the proceeds. The Chaoyang District People's Court sentenced Zhang to 12 years and 6 months in prison for robbery (抢劫罪), with deprivation of political rights, a fine of RMB 130,000, and an obligation to compensate the victim; the case was published as case No. 1569 of the Reference Compilation of Criminal Justice.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Simon Bolivar municipality (Rafael Urdaneta parish), Zulia State
description: On August 10, 2021, Gustavo Torres Gonzalez, 39, a computer engineer and owner of the wireless internet provider TutoNet Inversiones, was kidnapped as he arrived at his home in Simon Bolivar municipality (Zulia State). The kidnappers demanded a ransom payable exclusively in bitcoin, first 1.5 BTC then 0.5 BTC after negotiation, but the family could only raise 0.062 BTC (about USD 2,750) and then lost all contact with them. His body was found at dawn on August 11, 2021 on a road in Rafael Urdaneta parish, riddled with six bullets; the investigation was handed to the CICPC and no arrests had been reported, with the local press noting that the victim had no apparent connection to cryptocurrencies, the payment method having been imposed by the kidnappers.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On August 11, 2021, a gang nicknamed the "bakfietsbende" (cargo-bike gang) robbed the Soephuisstraat warehouse used by two coffeeshops in Groningen (Reykjavik and De Vliegende Hollander) and made off with part of the stock in cargo bikes. Shortly after, the manager received messages describing the robbery as a mere "warning" and demanding EUR 100,000 as well as "millions in bitcoins," failing which he would be shot and his family "wiped out." Placed in a safehouse by police, the victim carried out a controlled handover of EUR 100,000 at Sontplein, where a 25-year-old suspect from Purmerend was arrested; four men aged 24, 25, 31 and 35 (from Leeuwarden, Amsterdam, Purmerend) were prosecuted.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On February 22, 2022, around 5:30 p.m., Abdel Rahman Akkad, 27, from Amsterdam, entered the Apple Store on Leidseplein in Amsterdam armed with an automatic rifle and a handgun, took a 44-year-old British customer hostage and demanded the equivalent of 200 million euros in cryptocurrency, threatening to blow himself up (the 'explosives' turned out to be training equipment). He opened fire on police several times; the hostage situation lasted about five hours, roughly seventy people were evacuated around 8:30 p.m., and four remained hidden in a closet. Around 10:30 p.m. the hostage escaped, the hostage-taker chased him and was struck by a vehicle of the special intervention service (DSI); he died of his injuries, with no ransom having been paid.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: A wealthy merchant walking from his home in northern Tehran to his office was intercepted by a Peugeot carrying three occupants; two of them, posing as police officers, brandished a fake arrest warrant for 'participation in recent unrest' and forced him into the car. Under threat of death to him and his family - a third accomplice having been posted outside his home - the kidnappers took his bank cards and purchased about 1.5 billion tomans' worth of crypto-assets, then three hours later drove him to a currency exchange office in the capital to make him buy 2 billion tomans' worth of dollars. The exchange dealer, alerted by his pallor, trembling and stammering, called 110 from the back room on the pretext of fetching the currency from the safe and stalled the transaction: the police intervened, freed the victim and arrested the two main suspects.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: San Pedro de Montes de Oca, San José
description: On Wednesday 4 January 2023, Jorge "George" Angulo Solano, 45, was intercepted in the parking lot of his gym in San Pedro de Montes de Oca by four men who threatened him with assault rifles and forced him into a car. His family paid an undisclosed millionaire-sum ransom in bitcoin, and the victim was freed and picked up by OIJ agents on the night of Friday 6 January near Sarapiquí, on Route 32, after about two days in captivity. The public prosecutor's investigation subsequently implicated a 13-person structure with divided roles (intelligence, drivers, guards, wallet creators, and crypto-to-cash converters), led by Byron Estiben Madrigal Calvo and responsible for a second kidnapping in July 2023.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On Tuesday, June 27, 2023 in Escazu, entrepreneur Jaime Gurdian Moreno, 66, a former senior executive at multinational financial companies, was intercepted while driving his car by several armed men and held captive for three days. His family made two payments totaling 130 to 140 million colones (about USD 245,000) in bitcoins to wallets provided by the gang, and he was released in La Uruca on Friday, June 30, shortly before midnight. The indictment from the organized crime prosecutor's office (FAEDO) names 13 people for this kidnapping and that of entrepreneur George Angulo Solano in January 2023, with the gang split between a subgroup carrying out the abductions and another tasked with converting the bitcoins into USDT and then cash.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On July 7, 2023, a shopkeeper from Tehuacan was violently overpowered in her establishment by Dulce Yanett N. and another individual, then moved and held captive in a building in Colonia Nicolas Bravo. That same day, the kidnappers demanded that her family pay five million pesos in cryptocurrency. Agents from the prosecutor's office specializing in kidnappings located the victim's smartwatch through a tracking app, allowing her release on July 8, 2023 and the arrest of one of the participants; Dulce Yanett N., who had fled, was not arrested until March 2026, on a warrant issued on February 10, 2026 for aggravated kidnapping.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: For several months until late October 2023, a family from Collado Villalba was extorted by a group that threatened to physically attack the father and his relatives if he did not pay EUR 4 million in cryptocurrency, under a security contract that had never actually been agreed. A "security" phone was imposed on the victim so his communications could be monitored remotely. At the very moment the father filed a complaint with the Kidnapping and Extortion unit, one of the perpetrators entered the family home, where the minor daughter was alone, and used her phone to call the mother and ask where her husband was. The Policía Nacional intervened urgently and announced on December 19, 2023 the arrest of four people, apprehended in a vehicle whose trunk contained an axe, a large stick and a baseball bat; the ransom was never paid.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Manila (abduction); body found in San Simon, Pampanga
description: A Malaysian national working in Manila was abducted on October 22, 2023 and a ransom of MYR 330,000 was paid to the kidnappers the following day via a USDT cryptocurrency wallet app. On the same October 23, Philippine authorities reported the discovery of a body in San Simon (Pampanga) whose physical description and tattoo matched the victim. Referred on November 9 by the Malaysian police attache in Manila, Bukit Aman's commercial crime department (director Ramli Mohamed Yoosuf) traced the crypto flows to an exchange platform not registered in Malaysia, whose information allowed the identification of six suspects, all foreign nationals.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Welwyn Garden City (Brocket Hall Golf Club), Hertfordshire
description: On October 24, 2023 around 4:10 p.m., Dylan Huang, a Chinese businessman in his thirties working between London and Singapore, was abducted on the course of the Brocket Hall Golf Club (Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire) by five well-dressed men posing as Chinese police officers: one held him at gunpoint, his three female companions were sprayed in the face with a substance, and he was struck in the face and eyes before being thrown into a black Audi Q7 with cloned plates. Taken to a rented house in Thursley, near Guildford (Surrey), he was blindfolded, gagged and then locked for thirty hours in a cage too low to stand up in, denied access to a toilet, while his kidnappers demanded a ransom of USD 15 million (about GBP 12 million) in bitcoin. The ransom was never paid: Huang was released on October 25 around 11 p.m. near Silvermere Golf Club in Cobham (Surrey), one hour after the arrest of Tianfu Guo in Chinatown (London).
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On November 24, 2023 in Novorossiysk, three men who had been surveilling Yulia Grigorenko for weeks abducted her in the parking lot of her fitness club using a car stolen that same day (the owner having been tasered and locked in the trunk), took her into a forest and killed her with 15 stab wounds before hiding the body under branches. They then made her husband believe she was alive and demanded 26 bitcoins (approx. RUB 87 million) within ten days, threatening him if he alerted the FSB or the police. The organizer, Ridvan Aliev, 30, died of a heart attack after his arrest; Karen Toroyan and Ashot Agayan have been on trial in Krasnodar since 2025 (hearings set for July 30, 2026) and claim they acted on an alleged "order from the special services".
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Manila (arrival), region not specified for the captivity
description: Li Jia, a Chinese executive at a Germany-based company, and his friend Zhao Dong, of Chinese-Austrian background, were lured to the Philippines under the pretext of a fake business inspection trip and abducted shortly after their arrival on January 18, 2024. The kidnappers demanded 1.5 million USDT; Li's family paid 190,000 USDT split across several accounts despite police advice, and further demands followed, with the last contact from Li on January 26 and the last message from an intermediary on February 6, 2024. Neither man has ever been found, despite Chinese, Philippine, Austrian and German investigations.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Petrópolis, Rio de Janeiro; body found at the suspect's home
description: On 29 February 2024 at around 11:30 a.m., lawyer Anic de Almeida Peixoto Herdy, wife of Benjamim Cordeiro Herdy, one of the heirs of the Unigranrio university group, parked her car at a shopping center in Petrópolis and got into a black Jeep Compass. That evening her husband received a message demanding a ransom payable in bitcoin. Lourival Correa Netto Fadiga, an IT technician close to the couple who posed as a retired federal police officer and had installed their security cameras, acted as go-between "because he understood cryptocurrencies". The husband paid about BRL 4.6 million in total in dollars, reais and bitcoin, including 6.24 BTC (about BRL 2.2 million) according to Portal do Bitcoin, plus BRL 790,000 deposited on 8 March with a bitcoin-purchase intermediary. Anic was never released: Fadiga, her lover according to the police, confessed to killing her in a motel in the Petrópolis district; her body was found encased in concrete in his backyard on 25 September 2024.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On October 13, 2024 at around 5 a.m., a 59-year-old Malaysian property developer of Chinese descent was intercepted outside his home in Iskandar Puteri (Johor Bahru district) as he was waiting for a car to Senai Airport: masked men beat him with sticks, threatened him with a firearm, blindfolded him, chained him and held him captive in a dark room. The network, organized into three cells (planning/abduction, handling of stolen items, and ransom collection and conversion into cryptocurrency), demanded up to 30 million ringgit and ultimately obtained 20 million, part of it paid via a payment link provided by the kidnappers; the victim was released the same day, with police stating the release occurred around noon (about 7 hours of captivity). On October 30, police announced 14 suspects arrested (aged 23 to 58, including three Vietnamese nationals and a relative of the victim, with one suspect still at large) and the recovery of MYR 7.2 million: MYR 1.95 million in cash, SGD 1 million and 400,000 USDT (~MYR 1.756 million), as well as a Beretta automatic pistol and 250 rounds of ammunition.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Etten-Leur (abduction); held in Klundert (Moerdijk), North Brabant
description: On 21 November 2024 in Etten-Leur, a Chinese national living in North Brabant was abducted (taken out of a van) and driven to a warehouse, where he was moved to another car, then driven to a caravan site in Klundert. Drugged according to his account, he was chained to a post there with a blacked-out diving mask over his eyes, while his kidnappers (seven according to AD) demanded a ransom of one million euros in cryptocurrency (USD 1.5 million according to AD). As the ransom was not paid immediately, he was held for three to four days until a friend paid.
note: The crypto motive is not established: no source says the victim or the family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.
missing: A source establishing that the victim or the victim's family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.

description: An Afghan industrialist was abducted and held captive for 80 days in Mashhad by a gang of five Afghan nationals who subjected him to abuse and demanded his family pay 50,000 Tether for his release. The Mashhad judicial police freed him in a raid and arrested the five gang members, nicknamed by police the "Tether hostage-takers gang"; their interrogations uncovered other earlier crimes (the murder of an Afghan money changer and the kidnapping of two children in 2022). The captivity, which ended in mid-December 2024, had thus begun around late September 2024.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: Chinese national Ren Binglin was lured to Egypt with a fake IT job offer, then picked up as soon as he got off the plane at Cairo airport and taken to an apartment in Al-Rehab city, where he was tied up, gagged, blindfolded, beaten and threatened with shotguns, knives and an electric baton. His captors filmed him and sent the videos to his family via WeChat, demanding a ransom of 70,000 dollars, to be transferred in digital currencies according to the testimony of the secretary of the Chinese embassy. Alerted by the embassy, the Cairo police stormed the location and freed the hostage; five defendants (3 Chinese, 2 Egyptian) were sentenced to 15 years in prison on June 16, 2026 and three others were acquitted.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

city: Location not specified by sources (victim resident in Jeju, South Korea)
description: A Korean man in his twenties, resident in Jeju, who went to Cambodia in June 2025 after traveling to Busan to take out a loan, was held captive by a local criminal organization. He was only released after a ransom of about 35 million won in cryptocurrencies, demanded from his family, was paid, and he returned to Korea on 9 August 2025, suffering from psychological shock for which he is being treated. The complaint filed on 9 July 2025 at the Jeju-West police station and the request for cooperation sent to the Cambodian authorities have had no effect.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On July 24, 2025, a 51-year-old farm operator from Hubynykha was lured to a business meeting by two unknown men who handcuffed him, took his Volkswagen and drove him to Donetsk oblast, where he was held and mistreated while the kidnappers demanded USD 70,000 from his son to be paid into a cryptocurrency wallet, a method chosen to make tracing more difficult. Once the ransom was gathered and paid, the victim was released; the investigation, supported by the cyber police and traffic cameras, identified a 23-year-old former serviceman and a 24-year-old active-duty serviceman, who were placed in pretrial detention.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: Xu Yating, 25, arrived in Bangkok on September 18, 2025 for a work assignment and disappeared after leaving the airport by taxi. In late September, an unknown person contacted her family on WeChat, sent a video of the young woman sitting in the back of a vehicle, and demanded 30,000 USDT before October 5. A contact presenting himself as a former university classmate, who had approached her in February about a "tech park" and had her flight information, is suspected of having lured her into a scam compound in Southeast Asia.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: Ding Shi Zu, a Chinese national, was abducted by unknown individuals on 15 Mehr 1404 (October 7, 2025) just after leaving Tehran's Imam Khomeini Airport. His kidnappers sent his family images of him being tortured via a foreign messaging app, demanded USD 50,000 in Tether to be paid via Binance before 2 p.m. on 18 Mehr, and threatened to kill him and harvest his organs, including a kidney. Alerted by the Chinese embassy, the western Tehran judicial police identified the gang in under six hours and freed the hostage unharmed on October 10, 2025 in a town in western Tehran province, with all four kidnappers arrested.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On November 4, 2025 around 3 PM, an 8-year-old girl from the Gomari neighborhood in Maiduguri was kidnapped while returning from school: the kidnappers made her take several tricycles (Keke Napep) to obscure the route, had her change clothes at a tailor's, then hid her in a hotel in the Pompomari Bypass area with the complicity of Amina Ibrahim, who posed as her mother. The child was drugged and held for three days until the family paid a ransom of 3 million naira in cryptocurrency, and was released on November 7. Borno State police arrested five suspects between November 29 and December 4, 2025, including the victim's uncle Mustapha Mohammed (20), identified as the mastermind, and Lawan Yusuf Hassan (25), an IT technician who cashed the ransom.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On the night of November 30 to December 1, 2025, two Italian-speaking men with "Western features," posing as police officers, forced Yang Yixian, 46, a Chinese entrepreneur living in Empoli, into a large car as he left a karaoke bar in Prato; he was held for about a week in the basement of an apartment on Via Pistoiese. The family reportedly paid a ransom of about EUR 100,000 in bitcoin, transferred from one foreign account to another (China to China), and the victim was released on December 5 in Piazza Mercatale. Two Chinese nationals were placed in detention on December 13, 2025 during a raid on the place of confinement, and one of the alleged kidnappers (the one disguised as a police officer) was arrested in Bulgaria.
note: The crypto motive is not established: no source says the victim or the family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.
missing: A source establishing that the victim or the victim's family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.

city: Uberaba, Minas Gerais / arrest in Cravinhos, São Paulo
description: On December 15, 2025, a 67-year-old businessman from Uberaba (MG) was approached at his home by an individual who first posed as an insurance claims expert, then as a Federal Police agent; after reporting a fake problem with a wheel, the suspect displayed a weapon and forced him into his vehicle to Thomas Bawden Camargos Avenue, where he forced him to take part in a video call with his son, demanding BRL 9 million in cryptocurrency in exchange for his release. The victim was ultimately released without any payment being made. Alerted by the Minas Gerais Military Police, the Ribeirão Preto police intercepted the merchant Jamilton de Souza, 48, that same evening on the Anhanguera Highway (SP-330) in Cravinhos, carrying a fake firearm, a wallet bearing the Federal Justice emblem, and three phones.
note: The crypto motive is not established: no source says the victim or the family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.
missing: A source establishing that the victim or the victim's family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.

city: Catalina Foothills, Pima County (northern suburb of Tucson), Arizona
description: During the night of January 31 to February 1, 2026, Nancy Guthrie, 84, mother of Today Show host Savannah Guthrie, was forcibly abducted from her isolated home in Catalina Foothills, a northern suburb of Tucson (Pima County, Arizona), where she lived alone: her doorbell camera, unplugged at 1:47 a.m., filmed a masked, armed man, and investigators found signs of forced entry as well as blood matching the victim's DNA; she left behind her phone, wallet and car. Several handwritten or anonymous ransom notes were sent to the family and to Tucson media outlets (KGUN, KOLD, TMZ): the one dated February 2 demanded 4 million dollars in cryptocurrency with a threat that the amount would increase, others demanded 'several million dollars' in bitcoin with a crypto address and a deadline of February 9 under threat of death, while a note dated February 6 claimed the victim had died shortly after her abduction and was 'buried in the wild.' No ransom has been paid, the victim remains missing as of September 12, 2026, and no charges have been filed for the abduction, as the FBI judged several of the early notes to be fraudulent.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On the evening of August 2, 2026, on Friendship Highway in Angeles City (Pampanga), a 37-year-old Chinese businessman on vacation in the Philippines, whose family runs supermarkets in the country, was kidnapped by six armed men (five Chinese and one Filipino) traveling in a van. The kidnappers demanded a ransom of one million dollars payable in cryptocurrency. On August 4, the victim took advantage of his guards falling asleep after drinking to escape through a window and call for help; four suspects (three Chinese, one Filipino) were arrested and charged with kidnapping for ransom and serious illegal detention.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: A network made up of five Chinese nationals and one Malaysian of Chinese descent identified its victims on Telegram, WeChat and Badoo by promising them well-paid consultant jobs or a trip, then kidnapped them upon their arrival at Penang airport. A 33-year-old Chinese woman who arrived on August 5, 2026 was held captive in a house in Taman Amira in Alor Setar, chained and blindfolded, with the kidnappers demanding 20,000 USDT (about 82,000 ringgit) from her family while threatening to send her to Myanmar. During the raid on August 7 at 8:40 p.m., police came under gunfire, shot dead two kidnappers, and freed two hostages who had been wounded with a bladed weapon (her and a 72-year-old Singaporean retiree ransomed for SGD 1 million), before arresting six suspects in a neighboring house.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: In the early morning of September 8, 2026, a 41-year-old South Korean businessman was intercepted on Roxas Boulevard, near Vicente Sotto Street in Pasay City, by at least seven men in a silver SUV who forced him into their vehicle. The kidnappers demanded 30 million pesos from a relative; the family paid about 550,000 pesos, partly in Philippine pesos and partly in Tether (USDT). The victim was released shortly afterward in Kawit, Cavite, and returned to Pasay, where the PNP-AKG took charge of him; no suspect had been identified as of September 9, with police tracing the accounts that received the ransom.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: Piyush Savaliya, described as associated with BitConnect, was reportedly kidnapped in Gujarat, India, on 30 January 2018 and released two days later. The claim was made at a press conference by Shaktisinh Gohil, a spokesperson for the Congress party, who said the kidnapper was Shailesh Bhatt, a deceived BitConnect investor. Bhatt is also alleged to have extorted cryptocurrency and cash worth over Rs 155 crore (US$22 million) at gunpoint from Savaliya and another BitConnect man, Dhaval Mavani. How Savaliya was taken, where he was held and whether anything was obtained from him were not reported; a transfer of 2,256 bitcoins worth Rs 131 crore was attributed to Mavani. Gohil said the affair surfaced when Bhatt complained that Amreli district police had extorted 200 bitcoins (Rs 10 crore) from him. No arrest over Savaliya's kidnapping was reported.
note: Not excluded on the merits: the incident is crypto-related and physical. It is excluded because it rests on a single uncorroborated claim made at a party political press conference, with no police record, charge or conviction behind it, which fails the requirement for a credible published source.
missing: A police report, charge sheet or court document, rather than a single opposition-party press conference.

description: A 13-year-old boy was kidnapped near his home in Witbank, Mpumalanga, on 20 May 2018 as he walked back from a nearby spaza shop with a friend. A neighbour's CCTV camera caught part of the daylight kidnapping and showed the boy being forced into a silver Toyota Corolla. His parents went to the police station to report it and returned to find a ransom note in their yard demanding Bitcoin equivalent to R1.5m. The boy was reunited with his family unharmed a few days later; how his captivity ended was not stated and police did not disclose whether any ransom was paid. After months of investigation two men were arrested, one in November in Germiston, Gauteng, and the second in Ladysmith, KwaZulu-Natal, on 30 December, and both appeared in court in January 2019.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: On 21 August 2018, two men dragged a 13-year-old girl into their vehicle, a VW Polo, in Aerorand, Middelburg, Mpumalanga. She shouted for help, and a group of people working nearby heard her, came to her aid and helped her escape. The men fled and left the car behind with their belongings inside. Nothing was demanded or taken and no injury was reported. Police hold the same two men responsible for the 20 May 2018 kidnapping of a 13-year-old boy in Witbank, in which the ransom was demanded in Bitcoin, and suspect they planned the same had the abduction succeeded.
note: The crypto motive is not established: no source says the victim or the family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.
missing: A source establishing that the victim or the victim's family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.

description: A woman in Taichung owed her roommate, Chang Hsiu-chun, for rent and living costs Chang had paid for her. On the evening of August 3, 2023, Chang, her boyfriend Huang Chin-kai, a friend, Wang Tzu-hua, and two teenagers gathered in the shared flat, Huang carrying a gas pistol. Chang asked the woman by WeChat to come home, saying she felt unwell. When she arrived the door was locked, and Huang took her phone and passcode and used it to call her boyfriend. He was beaten with fists, a helmet and the gas pistol, and Wang made the couple slap themselves and each other. Told to pay TWD 100,000, the woman borrowed it from a friend abroad, who sent 3,160 USDT to Huang's wallet, and the group left. In July 2025 the Taichung District Court convicted the three adults of unlawful confinement with a weapon, finding the debt real.
note: The sources establish an aim other than obtaining cryptocurrency: a debt, a dispute or a business conflict.

description: Nate Geier, a co-founder of a software development company, was in Singapore for the Token2049 conference when he woke up in hospital with heavy bruising down the right side of his face and a cut on his nose. On 3 October 2025 he posted on X that he must have been jumped walking home after the event, that he remembered only waking up in hospital, and that his passport and ring were gone. He said it happened at 11pm. No attacker is described and no cryptocurrency is reported taken. Some people who replied to his post doubted he had been robbed, pointing to Singapore's CCTV coverage, and some speculated that he could have been drunk.
note: The crypto motive is not established: no source says the victim or the family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.
missing: A source establishing that the victim or the victim's family held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers sought it.

description: At about 8 p.m. on 29 May 2026, three men forced Yang Weixin, 53, a Chinese real estate developer living in Phnom Penh, from the parking area of his apartment building into a vehicle; the building's security cameras recorded the abduction. At about 3 a.m. on 30 May the kidnappers used his phone to demand $2 million in cryptocurrency from his wife, who told police she could not raise the money. No payment was reported. Roughly 14 hours after the abduction a truck driver found Yang's bloodstained car in Dangkao district, and police told the family he had been found dead; investigators found blood, knives, tape and plastic ties in and around the car. Cambodian police said he was tortured by three captors before being murdered. The three men remain at large.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: Harry Chun Tak Yeh, founder and managing partner of Quantum Fintech Group, was found dead at about 04:30 on 7 August 2026 outside the Jade Park tower in the Trinidad district of Asuncion, Paraguay. Officers answering an emergency call found his body at the base of the building, naked and covered with a black plastic bag; police said he had fallen from the 30th floor. A prosecutor who went up to the 30th-floor flat where he was believed to have lived found all the doors open, the flat turned over and nobody inside. His partner, who lived on the 27th floor, told officers she did not know what had happened. Nobody has been accused of involvement, no theft is confirmed and nothing is reported missing. Prosecutors were pursuing homicide, accident and suicide as parallel lines, and the autopsy was still pending.
note: No attack is established: police could not determine how he fell and treated homicide, accident and suicide as parallel hypotheses, with no theft confirmed, nothing reported missing and nobody accused.
missing: A source establishing that a physical attack took place, rather than an unexplained death.

city: Jundiaí (seized); Chácaras Campo Limpo, Campo Limpo Paulista, São Paulo (held)
description: On the afternoon of 16 September 2026, a 48-year-old businessman was seized in Jundiai, Brazil, while on the phone at his place of work. Two men armed with revolvers got out of a GM Astra and forced him into the car, where a third man was at the wheel. He was taken to a shack in woodland in Campo Limpo Paulista, where he was held for about three hours under threat of firearms and struck on the head. The men took his phone and demanded bank transfers by Pix to several accounts. When the bank blocked the account they tried 'Cripto-Pix' operations; no completed cryptocurrency transfer is reported. They also took jewellery, a watch, cash and his car key. The men fled after a lookout warned of police in the area, and the businessman escaped and found a police team; one suspect was detained on 24 September.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any.

description: A UK crypto trader known on X as 'Realist' says three intruders entered his home on the night of 12 October 2026. By his account they taped him up, held three knives to his face and said they would kill him unless he gave them his crypto. He says they took about $40,000 from his main wallets and $720,000 from a Ledger hardware wallet, plus a Rolex, and smashed his phone before fleeing; he first put the loss at about $800,000. On-chain records show the Solana address he flagged received about $756,000 in SOL and USDC that night and was emptied by 1:41 the next morning. He says he was left with bruises and that police attended and treated his home as a crime scene. Police have not confirmed his account and no arrests have been reported.
note: Not excluded on the merits: the account is crypto-related, physical and partly corroborated by on-chain movement. It is excluded because the incident is known only from the victim's own posts, with no police confirmation of the home invasion and no arrest.
missing: Police confirmation of the home invasion, rather than the victim's own posts alone.

city: Bali (abducted while motorcycling; villa in Tabanan searched)
description: Igor Komarov, 28, a Ukrainian, was abducted on 15 February 2026 while riding a motorcycle in Bali, where he was reportedly on holiday with his girlfriend, the influencer Eva Mishalova, and a friend, Yermak Petrovsky. Komarov's location was reportedly revealed by a geolocated photograph Mishalova posted on Valentine's Day. A video later appeared on Telegram in which Komarov, visibly bruised, says his legs and ribs are broken and some of his fingers have been cut off, and begs his parents to send $10 million to cryptocurrency wallets. Nothing was reported paid and authorities did not confirm the video's claims. Police traced a rental car to a villa in Tabanan, where they found his phone, his bag and blood traces. Body parts were later found at the mouth of the Wos River about 30 km away with tattoos partly matching his; police had not confirmed the identity and DNA tests were under way. Police arrested the man who rented the car and named six foreign nationals as suspects, all placed on an Interpol red notice.
note: Cryptocurrency was only a payment method imposed on someone not known to hold any: the victim was a tourist abducted off the street, no source says he held or was known to hold crypto, and the $10m figure comes from a ransom video that authorities did not confirm.
missing: A source establishing that the victim held cryptocurrency, or that the attackers targeted him for it rather than for a ransom payable in crypto.
